title: Rome in Seven Layers: Centro Storico to EUR

bestPeriod.avoid: August, 36 °C on unshaded travertine, half the good trattorie closed for *ferie*; and the Christmas-Epiphany fortnight, when the centre is impassable and museum slots vanish.

accommodation.note: Monti or Trastevere double, per-person share, €160, €280 per room per night

food.note: Trattoria dinner €30, €45, pizza al taglio lunch €6, €10, coffee standing €1.20

transport.note: Leonardo Express return, ATAC weekly CIS, Ostia Antica return

activities.note: Vatican, Colosseum, Borghese, Palazzo Massimo, Case Romane, Ostia Antica

profile.difficultyNote: 2/5-7-11 km of walking a day on cobbles and stairs, with the Gianicolo and Celio climbs the only real vertical

gatewayAirport: FCO Leonardo da Vinci-Fiumicino, Leonardo Express to Termini 32 min; CIA Ciampino for low-cost carriers, 40 min by bus
summary: Rome is not a city you see, it is a city you cross-section. This week takes seven cuts through it: the Baroque theatre of the Centro Storico, the imperial spine of Colosseum-Forum-Palatine, the Vatican, the Republican and Imperial sculpture at Palazzo Massimo, the working-class kitchen of Testaccio, the industrial archaeology of Ostiense, and Mussolini's white marble suburb at EUR, closing with a day at Ostia Antica, the port city that is Pompeii without the crowds. The single hardest skill is ticketing: four of the week's set pieces require timed slots bought on specific official platforms at specific moments, and the difference between doing that and not is roughly three hours of queuing per day. Walking is the transport of choice; the metro is only three lines and mostly goes where you are not.

itinerary.title: Arrival, Centro Storico, and the Pantheon at dusk
itinerary.morning: Leonardo Express in to Termini, drop bags in Monti, and take the first coffee standing at a bar counter, sitting doubles the price by law and everyone knows it.
itinerary.afternoon: Walk the Centro Storico spine: **Piazza Navona**, **Sant'Ivo alla Sapienza**'s courtyard, the **Pantheon**, then **San Luigi dei Francesi** for the three Caravaggios of the **Contarelli Chapel**, bring €1 coins for the light box, and go at a quiet hour.
itinerary.evening: **Ai Tre Scalini** on Via Panisperna in Monti, standing at the bar with a glass of Cesanese and a plate of *polpette*.
itinerary.dayStats: 7.2 km walking / 60 m ascent; Leonardo Express €14, 32 min; CIS weekly card €29; Pantheon timed entry required

itinerary.title: The imperial spine: Colosseum, Forum, Palatine, Celio
itinerary.morning: Pre-booked **Colosseum** slot as early as the ticket allows. The 24-hour ticket covers the Forum and Palatine as one continuous visit, enter the Colosseum first, then walk out to the Forum through the Arch of Titus side.
itinerary.afternoon: The **Palatine** for the Farnese gardens and the Domus Augustana, then down to the **Roman Forum**. Late afternoon, cross to the **Celio** for the **Case Romane del Celio** beneath Santi Giovanni e Paolo, a frescoed Roman apartment block under a church, closed Tuesdays and Wednesdays, and finish at **San Clemente**, three buildings stacked: a 12th-century basilica over a 4th-century church over a Mithraeum.
itinerary.evening: **La Carbonara** on Via Panisperna. Order the carbonara; it is the correct place to be obvious.
itinerary.dayStats: 9.4 km / 120 m ascent; Colosseum €18 + €2 booking, 24 h validity; Case Romane ≈€8; San Clemente lower levels ticketed

itinerary.title: Vatican Museums early, Prati afternoon
itinerary.morning: Earliest possible **Vatican Museums** entry, €20 plus the €5 booking fee. Go directly through the Pinacoteca or the Egyptian rooms to reach the **Sistine Chapel** before the group tours converge; then double back for the Raphael Rooms and the Gallery of Maps at leisure.
itinerary.afternoon: **St Peter's Basilica** (free, security queue) and the dome climb, 551 steps, or the lift plus 320. Then west into **Prati** and lunch standing at **Bonci Pizzarium** by Cipro.
itinerary.evening: **Il Sorpasso**, Via Properzio, Roman-Iberian, cured meats and *maritozzi*. Walk back across Ponte Sant'Angelo.
itinerary.dayStats: 8.6 km / 90 m ascent; Vatican €25 all-in; dome 551 steps; Prati grid 2.6 km

itinerary.title: Galleria Borghese and Palazzo Massimo
itinerary.morning: Your **Galleria Borghese** two-hour shift, booked, non-negotiable, and genuinely enough. Look at Bernini's *Apollo and Daphne* and *Ratto di Proserpina* (the fingers in the marble thigh), then the six Caravaggios.
itinerary.afternoon: Walk the **Villa Borghese** gardens down to the **Pincio** terrace and Piazza del Popolo, calling at **Santa Maria del Popolo** for the Cerasi Chapel Caravaggios. Then to **Palazzo Massimo alle Terme** by Termini for the Villa of Livia garden frescoes and the Boxer at Rest, the least-crowded great museum in Rome.
itinerary.evening: **Roscioli**, Via dei Giubbonari 21, booked. Burrata, anchovies, and a serious wine list.
itinerary.dayStats: 8.8 km / 70 m ascent; Borghese €13 + €2, two-hour slot, closed Mondays; Palazzo Massimo on the Museo Nazionale Romano combined ticket

itinerary.title: Testaccio, Ostiense and Roman industry
itinerary.morning: **Mercato Testaccio** before 11:00, the stalls, then a *trapizzino* or a *panino con allesso*. Walk to the **Piramide Cestia** (12 BC) and the **Cimitero Acattolico** for Keats and Shelley.
itinerary.afternoon: Down Via Ostiense to the **Centrale Montemartini**, classical marbles installed among the turbines and diesel engines of Rome's first public power station, and the best-staged museum in the city. Continue to the **Gazometro** and the Ostiense street art.
itinerary.evening: **Flavio al Velavevodetto**, Via di Monte Testaccio 97, in rooms cut into Monte dei Cocci, a 35 m hill made entirely of smashed Roman amphorae. Book.
itinerary.dayStats: 9.1 km / 50 m ascent; Mercato Testaccio Mon-Sat mornings; Montemartini open Tue-Sun; Metro B Piramide

itinerary.title: Ostia Antica day trip
itinerary.morning: Metro B to **Piramide**, cross to **Porta San Paolo**, and take the **Metromare** line to **Ostia Antica**, 25-35 minutes on a €1.50 BIT. Be at the gate for opening; the site is 150 hectares and there is almost no shade.
itinerary.afternoon: Work the Decumanus Maximus: the **Baths of Neptune** mosaics, the **theatre**, the **Piazzale delle Corporazioni** with its guild mosaics of ships and grain, the **Thermopolium** bar counter on Via di Diana, and the **Casa di Diana** insula. Four hours minimum. Bring water, refill points are limited.
itinerary.evening: Back into the city; dinner at **Da Enzo al 29** in Trastevere if you can face the queue, otherwise **Nannarella** on Piazza San Calisto.
itinerary.dayStats: 10.5 km walked at the site / return transit ≈70 min total / BIT €1.50 covers the whole journey / Ostia Antica entry ticket, sold by CoopCulture

itinerary.title: EUR, Trastevere and the Gianicolo
itinerary.morning: Metro B to **EUR Magliana/EUR Palasport** for the **Palazzo della Civiltà Italiana**, the **Palazzo dei Congressi** and the laghetto. An hour of white travertine, straight lines and total silence, the deliberate opposite of everything else this week.
itinerary.afternoon: Back to **Trastevere**: **Santa Maria in Trastevere** for the 12th-century apse mosaics and Cavallini's cycle, **Santa Cecilia** for the Cavallini Last Judgement, then up to **Bramante's Tempietto** at San Pietro in Montorio and the **Gianicolo** terrace.
itinerary.evening: **Antico Arco** on the Gianicolo for a proper last dinner, or a €3 negroni at **Bar San Calisto** and pizza at **Ai Marmi**.
itinerary.dayStats: 9.8 km / 130 m ascent (Gianicolo climb 2 km at 70 m); EUR by Metro B, 20 min from Termini
itinerary.sleep: Small hotel in Monti, or airport-side for an early flight

accommodationStrategy.name: Small hotel in Monti
accommodationStrategy.description: The best all-round base: ten minutes' walk to the Colosseum, twelve to Termini for the Leonardo Express, and a neighbourhood with its own bars and market rather than a museum queue. Streets are steep and cobbled, so a wheeled case is a genuine consideration. €160, €260 per room per night in shoulder season.

accommodationStrategy.name: A Trastevere guesthouse
accommodationStrategy.description: Right for a second visit or a trip weighted to the Vatican and the Gianicolo, and served directly by the FL1 regional train from Fiumicino at €8. The trade-off is noise: the Piazza Trilussa-San Calisto axis is loud until 02:00 at weekends, so ask for a courtyard room. €150, €240 per room.

accommodationStrategy.name: A Prati apartment
accommodationStrategy.description: Quiet, residential, on a grid, with the Mercato Trionfale and Via Cola di Rienzo for self-catering, and Cipro/Ottaviano metro for everything else. It is the sensible choice for a family or anyone who wants a kitchen and a lift. €140, €220 per apartment.

logistics.connectivity: EU roaming applies with no surcharge. 4G/5G is excellent everywhere including underground on Metro A and B. Free municipal WiFi (*DigitRoma WiFi*) exists in many piazzas and is slow. Download an offline map anyway: the Centro Storico's alleys defeat GPS.
logistics.emergency: 112 for everything (Italy's single European emergency number). Pharmacies rotate a *farmacia di turno* overnight, posted on every pharmacy door. Italy is in the EU, so **EHIC/GHIC covers state care**; the main central hospitals are Ospedale Fatebenefratelli on Tiber Island and Policlinico Umberto I near Termini.
logistics.weather: Rome's real hazard is heat, not storms, July and August routinely hit 35-38 °C with the *ponentino* evening breeze the only relief, and Ostia Antica and the Forum are entirely unshaded. Autumn brings short, violent *acquazzoni* that flood cobbled streets in twenty minutes and stop taxi availability dead. Winter is mild and wet; January averages 12 °C.
logistics.bookingWindows: Vatican Museums 4-8 weeks. Colosseum on the 30-day rolling release at 09:00 CET, this is the single most time-critical booking of the week. Galleria Borghese 3-5 weeks. Armando al Pantheon and Da Felice several weeks. Roscioli, La Carbonara, Flavio 3-7 days. Case Romane and Palazzo Massimo, days or same-day.
logistics.money: Euro. Cards are accepted almost universally and merchants are legally required to accept them, but small trattorie and market stalls still prefer cash, carry €50, €100. **Tipping is not expected**; a *coperto* of €1.50, €3 per person appears on the bill instead, and *servizio* is occasionally added, check before adding anything.
logistics.transportRules: Validate paper tickets before boarding; contactless card taps at metro gates charge the BIT rate automatically. The historic centre is a **ZTL (Zona a Traffico Limitato)** with camera enforcement and automatic fines, **do not hire a car for this itinerary**. Taxis must use the metered fare within the city and the fixed €55/€40 airport fares to and from the walls; ranks are safer than hailing. Metro A closes early (around 21:00) on some nights for works, replaced by the MA bus.
logistics.permits: Rome's **city tourist tax** is charged per person per night by hotel category, roughly €4, €10, usually payable in cash at check-out. Sitting on the Spanish Steps, eating on church steps, and wading in fountains are all finable under municipal decorum rules and are actively policed. Drones are banned over the historic centre. Large backpacks are refused at the Vatican Museums and the Colosseum; cloakrooms are free but slow.
logistics.health: Tap water is excellent and free, the **nasoni**, the cast-iron street fountains, run continuously and are potable; block the spout hole with a finger and it arcs upward to drink from. Rome is a low-violence, high-pickpocket city: Termini, the 64 bus to the Vatican, Metro A and the Colosseum forecourt are the specific hotspots. Wear real shoes; the *sampietrini* cobbles are ankle-hostile and lethal in rain.

proTips: **Set an alarm for the Colosseum's 30-day release at 09:00 CET.** CoopCulture is the only official seller; everything else is a reseller charging a markup for the same slot. Buy the moment your date opens, and take the earliest entry offered.
**Buy the CIS weekly card at €29 on day one.** It beats seven Roma 24H passes, covers the Metromare line to Ostia Antica, and removes every decision about whether a bus is worth €1.50.
**The Colosseum ticket is valid 24 hours.** Do the Colosseum in the evening and the Forum and Palatine the next morning on the same ticket, and you avoid the worst of both crowds.

**At the Vatican, walk away from the Sistine first.** Everyone funnels straight down the Candelabra-Tapestries-Maps corridor. Go via the Pinacoteca or the Egyptian collection, hit the chapel from the far side, then walk the corridors backwards when they have emptied.
**Use the nasoni.** Around 2,500 of them run across the city with free, cold, potable water. In August this saves you €20 a day and a great deal of misery.
**Eat lunch standing.** Pizza al taglio is sold by weight, point, say *basta* when the slice is the right size, pay €6, €10, and put the ninety minutes into the Palatine instead.

**Go to Ostia Antica, not Pompeii.** It is 35 minutes each way on a €1.50 city ticket rather than a day on a train, it is bigger than most people expect, and on a Tuesday in October you will have whole streets to yourself.
**Book Galleria Borghese for the 09:00 shift.** Two hours is a hard limit and the rooms are small; the first shift gives you Bernini's *Daphne* without a phone in front of it.

**Check the Case Romane del Celio calendar before you plan Day 2.** It closes Tuesdays and Wednesdays, and it is the best small ancient site in Rome, a frescoed Roman house, complete, under a working basilica.
**Take one hour in EUR.** Nowhere else shows you what the twentieth century wanted to do to Rome, and the Metro B ride out is twenty minutes.

raw.Centro Storico: Piazza Navona → Corso del Rinascimento → Pantheon → Via del Corso → Piazza di Spagna, a 2.4 km spine with every Baroque set piece hung off it; add the Campo de' Fiori-Via Giulia loop for another 1.8 km.
raw.Monti: Via Nazionale → Via Panisperna → Via dei Serpenti → Piazza della Madonna dei Monti → Via Leonina, ≈1.3 km of the oldest surviving street grid in the city, all of it uphill from the Forum.
raw.Trastevere: Piazza Trilussa → Via del Moro → Piazza Santa Maria in Trastevere → Via della Lungaretta → Piazza San Cosimato, 1.5 km flat, plus the Gianicolo climb (2 km, 70 m ascent) for the terrace view.
raw.Testaccio: Piramide → Via Marmorata → Mercato Testaccio → Via di Monte Testaccio → the Mattatoio, 1.7 km, flat and entirely without tourists before noon.
raw.Ostiense: Piramide → Via Ostiense → Centrale Montemartini → Gazometro, 2.2 km of street art and gas holders.
raw.Prati: Piazza Cavour → Via Cola di Rienzo → Mercato Trionfale → Via della Meloria, 2.6 km on a Haussmann-style grid, the antidote to the medieval tangle.
raw.EUR: Palazzo della Civiltà Italiana → Viale della Civiltà del Lavoro → Palazzo dei Congressi → the laghetto, 1.9 km of monumental rationalism on empty boulevards.
raw.Transit products and exact fares: ATAC's integrated Metrebus tickets: **BIT €1.50** (100 minutes, one metro entry, unlimited surface changes), **Roma 24H €8.50**, **Roma 48H €15.00**, **Roma 72H €22.00**, and the **CIS weekly card €29.00**, valid to midnight of the seventh day including the day of validation. All are valid on metro lines A/B/B1/C, buses, trams, the Metromare (ex Roma-Lido) line and regional trains inside the city boundary. Contactless bank cards work directly at metro gates and on many buses at BIT rates. For a full week, the **CIS at €29 beats seven day passes outright**.
raw.Airport transfer options and cost: **Leonardo Express**, FCO → Roma Termini non-stop, **32 minutes, €14**, roughly every 15 minutes 06:23-23:23, the reliable default. **FL1 regional train**, FCO → Trastevere / Ostiense / Tuscolana / Tiburtina, **€8**, better if you are sleeping in Trastevere or Testaccio. **Taxi from FCO** to any address inside the Aurelian Walls is a **fixed municipal fare of €55**, luggage included, insist on the flat fare, do not accept the meter. **Ciampino (CIA)**: Terravision/SIT coach to Termini, roughly **€6, €7, 40 minutes**; taxi flat fare inside the walls **€40**.
raw.Vatican Museums & Sistine Chapel: , museivaticani.va only. Standard admission **€20 plus a €5 online booking fee (€25 total)**. Closed Sundays except the last Sunday of the month (free, and unbearable). Book **4-8 weeks ahead** for spring; the early-entry and "Breakfast in the Museums" products release on the same site and go first.
raw.Colosseum, Roman Forum & Palatine: , coopculture.it, the only official seller. The **24-hour ticket is €18 plus a €2 booking fee**; the Full Experience with Arena and Underground costs more and is separately capped. Tickets release on a **rolling 30-day window at 09:00 CET** and high-season dates are gone in minutes. Set an alarm.
raw.Galleria Borghese: , galleriaborghese.beniculturali.it. **€13 plus a €2 mandatory booking fee**, Tuesday-Sunday 09:00-19:00, entry in hourly shifts with a **strict two-hour visit** (the 17:45 last shift is shorter and reduced to €8). Booking is compulsory even for free-entry categories. Book **3-5 weeks ahead**.
raw.Case Romane del Celio: , caseromane.it, around €8, **closed Tuesdays and Wednesdays**, small and rarely full; 2-3 days is enough.
raw.Palazzo Massimo alle Terme: , part of the Museo Nazionale Romano combined ticket covering Palazzo Altemps, the Terme di Diocleziano and Crypta Balbi over several days. Same-day entry is normally fine.
raw.Named architectural focal points, and wh: The **Pantheon** (Hadrian, 118-128 AD), stand under the 43.3 m coffered concrete dome and find the drainage holes in the floor beneath the oculus. **Sant'Ivo alla Sapienza** (Borromini, 1642-60), the spiral lantern, best seen from the courtyard. **San Carlo alle Quattro Fontane** (Borromini, 1638-41), an oval dome on a site the size of a Vatican pier. **Sant'Andrea al Quirinale** (Bernini, 1658-70), the reply, in pink marble. **Piazza Navona** (Bernini's Four Rivers, 1651) sits on the footprint of Domitian's stadium; the piazza *is* the arena. **Il Tempietto** at San Pietro in Montorio (Bramante, 1502), the moment the Renaissance stops quoting antiquity and starts equalling it. **Palazzo della Civiltà Italiana** at EUR (Guerrini, La Padula and Romano, 1938-43), the "Square Colosseum", six arches by nine, now Fendi's headquarters. **Ara Pacis Museum** (Richard Meier, 2006), the first new building in the historic centre since the war, and still argued about. **MAXXI** (Zaha Hadid, 2010) in Flaminio, and **Auditorium Parco della Musica** (Renzo Piano, 2002) next door.
notes: *Centro Storico:* **Armando al Pantheon**, Salita dei Crescenzi 31, €40, €55, book **weeks** ahead, tiny. **Roscioli Salumeria con Cucina**, Via dei Giubbonari 21, €45, €60, booking essential. **Antico Forno Roscioli** next door for pizza bianca, €4, €8, no booking. **Sant'Eustachio Il Caffè** for the *gran caffè*, €1.50 standing.

*Monti:* **La Carbonara**, Via Panisperna 214, €30, €40, book. **Ai Tre Scalini**, Via Panisperna 251, wine bar, €20, €30, no booking, arrive before 20:00. **Mercato Monti Urban Market**, Via Leonina 46, weekends only.

*Trastevere:* **Da Enzo al 29**, Via dei Vascellari 29, €25, €35, minimal reservations and a permanent queue; go at 19:00 sharp. **Antico Arco** on the Gianicolo, €50, €70, book. **Bar San Calisto** for a €3 negroni among Romans.

*Testaccio:* **Da Felice a Testaccio**, Via Mastro Giorgio 29, €35, €45, **book well ahead**, cacio e pepe tossed at the table. **Flavio al Velavevodetto**, Via di Monte Testaccio 97, €30, €40, dining rooms cut into a hill of Roman amphora shards, book. **Trapizzino**, Via Giovanni Branca 88, €4, €6 a pocket. **Mercato Testaccio**, Via Beniamino Franklin, Mon-Sat mornings. **Volpetti**, Via Marmorata 47, for cheese.

*Prati:* **Bonci Pizzarium**, Via della Meloria 43 by Cipro metro, €8, €15, standing, no booking. **Il Sorpasso**, Via Properzio 31-33, €25, €35. **Mercato Trionfale**, Via Andrea Doria, Mon-Sat, the largest covered market in the city.
*Ostiense:* **Porto Fluviale**, Via del Porto Fluviale 22, €25, €35, book at weekends.
raw.Day trip with exact line, time and fare: **Ostia Antica**, Metro B to **Piramide**, cross to the adjacent **Roma Porta San Paolo** station, take the **Metromare (ex Roma-Lido) line** toward Cristoforo Colombo, alight at **Ostia Antica**, roughly **25-35 minutes**. The whole journey is **inside the urban fare zone and covered by a €1.50 BIT** or any Roma pass, no separate ticket. The excavations are a 5-minute signed walk over the footbridge.

sources.confidenceNotes: Re-verify before publishing, (1) the **Colosseum €2 booking fee and the exact 30-day release mechanism**, which CoopCulture has changed more than once and which differs between the standard and Full Experience products; (2) **Ostia Antica's current admission price**, which has moved substantially in recent seasons and varies between high and low season, treat any figure as provisional; (3) the **Museo Nazionale Romano combined ticket price and validity period** covering Palazzo Massimo, Palazzo Altemps, Terme di Diocleziano and Crypta Balbi; (4) **Case Romane del Celio** admission and its Tuesday/Wednesday closure, which has varied; (5) **Pantheon** timed-entry pricing and any exemptions, introduced recently and still being adjusted; (6) **Roma Pass** 48h/72h pricing, deliberately omitted from the budget above because it rarely beats the CIS plus individual tickets on this itinerary, confirm before recommending it; (7) **Leonardo Express €14 and the €55/€40 fixed taxi fares**, both set by decree and periodically revised; (8) restaurant reservation policies, particularly **Da Enzo al 29**, which changes its walk-in rules seasonally; (9) Rome's **city tourist tax bands**, revised in recent budgets.
